name: Yaru
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Chapacuran; only Loukotka 1963 vocabulary; no stress description exists

new_statements.quote: Nas línguas Chapakura, a acentuação dos lexemas é dedutível do peso silábico - o único fator prosódico fonológico nessa família lingüística. Portanto, o acento não é fonológico por ser previsível. [...] A atualização fonética da acentuação lexical obedece às seguintes regras: (a) uma sílaba leve é átona e possui um tom baixo. [...] (b) uma sílaba pesada é tônica e possui um tom alto. [...] / # (σ) σ # / → [ (σò) » σè ] (p. 23). [p. 22:] O fator demarcativo do lexema é, portanto, o peso silábico, uma vez que uma sílaba pesada caracteriza sempre o final de um lexema, ao passo que uma sílaba leve caracteriza sempre a primeira sílaba de um lexema dissílabo.
new_statements.translation: In the Chapakura languages, the accentuation of lexemes is deducible from syllable weight – the only phonological prosodic factor in this language family. Therefore the accent is not phonological, since it is predictable. [...] The phonetic realization of lexical accentuation obeys the following rules: (a) a light syllable is unstressed and has a low tone. [...] (b) a heavy syllable is stressed and has a high tone. [...] /#(σ)σ#/ → [(σ̀) ˈσ́] (p. 23). [p. 22:] The demarcative factor of the lexeme is therefore syllable weight, since a heavy syllable always characterizes the end of a lexeme, whereas a light syllable always characterizes the first syllable of a disyllabic lexeme.
new_statements.citation: Angenot, Geralda de Lima Vitor. 2013 [1997]. Fonotática e fonologia do lexema protochapakura. Revista Eletrônica Língua Viva 3(1), Série de e-books & e-documentos, 159 pp. (originally MA thesis, Universidade Federal de Rondônia, 1997)
new_statements.locator: ch. 2.1.1 p. 22 and ch. 2.2 'A estrutura prosódica do lexema' p. 23 (PDF pp. 22-23); Yaru section 3.10 pp. 56-57
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (159 pp., text layer; printed page = PDF page). PDF p. 23, section 2.2 'A ESTRUTURA PROSÓDICA DO LEXEMA', reads exactly: 'Nas línguas Chapakura, a acentuação dos lexemas é dedutível do peso silábico - o único fator prosódico fonológico nessa família lingüística. Portanto, o acento não é fonológico por ser previsível.'... 'A atualização fonética da acentuação lexical obedece às seguintes regras: (a) uma sílaba leve é átona e possui um tom baixo. [...] (b) uma sílaba pesada é tônica e possui um tom alto. [...] / # (σ) σ # / → [ (σò) » σè ]'. PDF p. 22 (end of 2.1.1) reads exactly: 'O fator demarcativo do lexema é, portanto, o peso silábico, uma vez que uma sílaba pesada caracteriza sem…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level (pan-Chapakura) claim: stress is non-contrastive and falls on the heavy syllable (CVC or CV:); lexemes are either a single heavy syllable or light+heavy, so the stressed syllable is always the final syllable of the lexeme (weight-driven, equivalent to lexeme-final stress). For Yaru the author gives no separate rule; the 1927 Barbosa wordlist (Rondon & Faria 1948, p. 203 ff.) carries accent marks that are almost all final (tocotepací, tiprací, itiçí, trauanací), consistent with the family rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed; multi-lexeme phonological words in casual registers may fuse (p. 22), but no secondary stress is described.
new_statements.exceptions: None for lexemes; in casual (hypo-articulated) registers vowel shortening and fusion of monosyllabic lexemes can obscure the demarcation (p. 22-23). The author admits (p. 8) that Yaru's phonology was never described and her Yaru sketch depends on old orthographies.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the lexeme (morphological word) in maxi-articulated citation pronunciation; the statement is a comparative generalization over the whole Chapacuran family, supported instrumentally for living languages (Moré, Oro Win, Wari' etc.) but applied to Yaru only by inference from a 276-word 1927 list. Not a first-hand Yaru-specific description.
new_statements.identity_note: Yaru = Jarú/Yarú of the Jaru River, Rondônia (Glottolog yaru1257, no ISO code), sister of Urupá (urup1244 branch). Nimuendajú 1925:139-140,159 treats Jarú as the same language as Urupá with minor dialectal/pronunciation differences. Angenot 2013's stress statement is about the whole Chapacuran family (chap1271), not Yaru specifically; her Yaru section draws only on Barbosa's 1927 list in Rondon & Faria 1948.

sources.note: Ch. 2.2 (p. 23): in all Chapakura languages lexical stress is predictable from syllable weight (heavy syllable = stressed + high tone; light = unstressed + low tone), lexemes being a heavy monosyllable or light+heavy disyllable, so the final syllable is stressed. Ch. 3.10 'Fonemas e sons do Yaru' (pp. 56-57, source Barbosa 1948 [1927]) gives phonemes and allophones only, with no Yaru-specific stress statement; p. 8 admits Yaru's phonology was never described and her sketch rests on old orthographies.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1963. Documents et vocabulaires inédits de langues et de dialectes sud-américains. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 52: 7-60. doi:10.3406/jsa.1963.2001
sources.note: Section 15 'Yarú' pp. 19-20: 36-word list from an anonymous SPI manuscript ('Vocabulario Iarú', bibliography no. 6) set beside Urupá; forms carry acute accents (kotoá, kosagái, tekisí, katimasí, nikakú) but nothing is said about accent or stress.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1925. As tribus do alto Madeira. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 17: 137-172.
sources.note: 'Os Jarú' pp. 139-140: language differs from Urupá only in some dialectal forms (no Jarú vocabulary given). After the Urupá vocabulary, p. 159: 'Os Jarú fallam a mesma lingua, com diminuta differença no sotaque' (accent = pronunciation, not word stress). Notation key: acute = stressed vowel, ú = stressed long vowel, in the Urupá list only.

sources.citation: Birchall, Joshua, Michael Dunn & Simon J. Greenhill. 2016. A combined comparative and phylogenetic analysis of the Chapacuran language family. International Journal of American Linguistics 82(3): 255-284. doi:10.1086/687383
sources.note: States that the only Jarú language data were collected in 1927 by the Rondon Commission (Rondon & de Faria 1948) and that there are no remaining speakers; segmental correspondences only, no stress discussion (the word 'accent' appears only in the Nimuendajú 1925:159 quotation).

sources.citation: Rondon, Cândido M. S. & João Barbosa de Faria. 1948. Glossário geral das tribos silvícolas de Mato-Grosso e outras da Amazônia e do Norte do Brasil (Publicação 76, Anexo 5, Etnografia, Tomo I). Rio de Janeiro: Imprensa Nacional / CNPI.
sources.note: Only primary Jaru data (276 words per Angenot): comparative column 'Jaru, Urupá, Uómo, Pacaá-Novo' from p. 117 and 'Vocabulário dos índios Jarú, Urupá, Uómo e Pacaá-Novo' (J. Barbosa with the Jaru informant Araguí, Colônia Rodolfo Miranda, 25 Jan 1927) from p. 203. Editorial note IV p. 12 says the accent marks on vowels 'corresponde aos sons fortes e longos de sílabas tônicas'; the Jaru forms are marked almost uniformly on the final syllable (iuhenecí, tocotepací, tiprací, itiçí, trauanací, craticí). Raw data, no rule stated.
